verdict.rationale: Elicit documents a first-party API covering paper search, automated research reports, and end-to-end Systematic Reviews, and all API functionality is also exposed through its MCP server. However, nothing shows the API reaching UI parity: the Library, Collections, tags, alerts and Routines, the Research Agent, chat, skills, collaboration, and imports are documented only as UI features, and no OpenAPI spec was found. Missing for 10: evidence of API coverage for Library/Collections/tags management, Research Agent sessions and chat, alerts/Routines, skills, collaboration/sharing, Zotero/RIS imports, and column-level extraction control; a published API reference/OpenAPI spec; independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Elicit API lets you access Elicit's research capabilities programmatically: search 138 million+ academic papers and generate automated research reports from your own code, scripts, and workflows.
Systematic Review: run a full review end to end, with control over search strategy, screening criteria, extraction parameters, and reporting.
All API functionality is also available via MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, enabling use from Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and other MCP-compatible clients.
